## What it is

Collabora Online is an office suite in the browser: documents, spreadsheets and presentations, based on LibreOffice. CODE (Collabora Online Development Edition) is its free build ([CollaboraOnline/online](https://github.com/CollaboraOnline/online)). It does not keep files itself: a file app such as Nextcloud stores them and asks Collabora to open them through the WOPI protocol. It is the Supply Depot's office suite (issue #129, NMD-04).

**Why Collabora and not OnlyOffice:** Collabora's server code carries an MPL-2.0 notice (file-level copyleft, Market class L1), and its upstream Helm chart documents a non-root, no-capability setup that fits OneMind's rules. OnlyOffice was not evaluated in this PR.

**Licence:** `MPL-2.0`. `COPYING` in CollaboraOnline/online is the MPL-2.0 notice (read 2026-11-19), but GitHub's licence API reports `NOASSERTION` for the repository and the research licence matrix has no row, so the licence gate cannot confirm it (below). UNVERIFIED: the CODE image also bundles LibreOffice core and other components with their own licences, and CODE is a development edition with Collabora's own usage terms; neither was checked here.

**Icon:** a neutral generated icon with initials; no upstream logo is shipped.

## How it runs here

- One `Deployment`, one container: `docker.io/collabora/code:26.04.6.1.1`, pinned by digest (Docker Hub registry API, 2026-11-19; amd64 and arm64). The image runs `coolwsd` as UID 1001 on port 9980.
- **Restricted mode, from upstream:** the settings come from the "OpenShift quickstart" in the upstream Helm chart README (`kubernetes/helm/collabora-online/README.md`, commit `c662f7eb883d`): non-root, RuntimeDefault seccomp, all capabilities dropped, and `extra_params` that turn off TLS inside the cluster (`--o:ssl.enable=false --o:ssl.termination=false`), turn off coolwsd's use of Linux capabilities (`--o:security.capabilities=false`) and move its working folders to `/tmp`, which is a writable 2Gi `emptyDir`.
- **The trade-off, in plain words:** normally coolwsd uses root-like capabilities to put each open document in its own small jail (chroot). Without capabilities it cannot, so all documents open inside the same container. That container is still non-root, has no capabilities and is confined to its own namespace.
- No admin console: it needs a username and password, and committed manifests never carry secrets. No WOPI host allow-list (`aliasgroup1`) is set yet: it must name the file app that may use it, and that is set when a file app is paired with it.
- Probes: `GET /` (it answers `OK`; the path upstream's chart uses).
- Requests 200m CPU / 512Mi, limit 2 CPU / 2Gi: OneMind choices (the chart sets none).

## First run

Source: [CODE Docker image docs](https://sdk.collaboraonline.com/docs/installation/CODE_Docker_image.html).

Collabora is not used on its own: a file app (for example Nextcloud with its Office app) is pointed at `http://collabora-code.app-collabora-code.svc:9980`, and Collabora's `aliasgroup1` must name that file app. That pairing is not packaged yet.

## Why this app is blocked

The licence gate (`sdk/tools/app-gate` check 2, contract §9.4) accepts a licence only when GitHub's licence API or a research licence-matrix row confirms it. For `CollaboraOnline/online`, GitHub reports `NOASSERTION` and the matrix has no row, so the gate classes the licence as blocked. The gate was not changed. To unblock: add a research licence-matrix row for Collabora Online with the `COPYING` permalink (and a check of the bundled components and the CODE usage terms), then rerun the gate.

**Hold (ma/market-bump-45-blocked-app-images, 2026-11-27, Refs #1232, Refs #234):** not bumped in this change: the licence is not confirmed by the licence gate (GitHub reports NOASSERTION and there is no matrix row; see the licence notes). The CI gate decides the tier.
